record.final_answer:
Based on the retrieved textbook evidence, the provided excerpts mention that mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration in all major lineages of eukaryotes (*Biology, 23.1. Eukaryotic Origins, p.601*), evolved via endosymbiosis (*Biology, Glossary, p.628*), can increase in number through endurance training to enable more aerobic metabolism and ATP production (*Anatomy and Physiology, 10.6. Exercise and Muscle Performance, p.428*), and are contained within fungal cells (*Biology, 24.1. Characteristics of Fungi, p.633*). 

However, the provided textbook evidence **does not** contain a dedicated description of the detailed internal structure (such as cristae, matrix, or inner/outer membranes) or a comprehensive breakdown of the structural-functional relationship of the mitochondrion.

record.final_answer:
According to the textbook *Anatomy and Physiology*, the thyroid gland secretes the following hormones and main effects:

* **Thyroxine ($\text{T}_4$) and triiodothyronine ($\text{T}_3$)**: These amine hormones stimulate the basal metabolic rate (Anatomy and Physiology, 17.2. Hormones, p.736; Anatomy and Physiology, 17.5. The Parathyroid Glands, p.756).
* **Calcitonin**: This peptide hormone reduces blood $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ levels by inhibiting osteoclast activity, increasing osteoblastic activity, decreasing intestinal calcium absorption, and increasing calcium loss in the urine (Anatomy and Physiology, 17.5. The Parathyroid Glands, p.756; Anatomy and Physiology, 17.6. The Adrenal Glands, p.759).
